summary: Weijue Shi was a Buddhist studies figure who was ordained under Linyuan in 1963, studied with Lingshuan, and studied under Lingyuan (~1963–1970). He founded Lin Quan Temple in 1987, Chung Tai Shan, and Chung Tai Buddhist Institute in 1993.

Weiqiang Wang works in linguistics, Tibetology, and archaeology/history. He earned a PhD from Guangdong University of Foreign Studies (2009–2013), where he was a teacher/associate professor in 2005, and was attested as a researcher at China Tibetology Research Center in 2012.
Weirong Shen works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He held a teaching post at the University of Hong Kong and served at Renmin University of China (~2006–2014).
Weiru Guan is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2011).

Weizhong Huang specializes in Tibetology and archaeology/history. He held a post at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2012) and was attested as a professor at Renmin University of China in 2026.

Weldon South Coblin specializes in Sinology, linguistics, and Tibetology. He studied under Fang-Kuei Li (~1968–1972) and spent his career at the University of Iowa as Professor (~1973–2014) and Professor Emeritus of Chinese (~2014).

Wen-ling Jane specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under Lozang Jamspal and earned a PhD from Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman (attested 2009).

Wenbiao Mai works in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Hamburg, Kyoto University, and Peking University, where he earned a PhD, and held a post as a visiting assistant professor at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

Wendi L. Adamek specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies, earning a PhD from Stanford in 1998 under teachers Michel Strickmann, Seizan Yanagida, and Hidehiko Koga. She held posts at Barnard College (attested 2008) and University of Calgary (attested 2018–2026).

Wendy Doniger specializes in Indology, religious studies, and history. She studied at Radcliffe, Harvard (PhD under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, ~1963–1968), and Oxford (D.Phil. under Robert Charles Zaehner, ~1968–1973), later serving at the University of Chicago from 1978.
Wenjiang Ding worked in history and archaeology. He was a student of Qichao Liang, studied at Peking University, and later held a post at Peking University (~1931–1933).

Wenjie Duan was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Sichuan Fine Arts Institute (~1940–1945) and Central Academy of Fine Arts. He served at the Dunhuang Academy from 1946, eventually becoming director (1991) and honorary director (~1998).

Wenjie Qin works in Buddhist and religious studies. Qin earned a PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Wei-ming Tu, and was taught by Diana L. Eck, Masatoshi Nagatomi, Charles Hallisey, and Robert M. Gimello.
Wenzhuo Shi works in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Shi has been a PhD student and researcher at Ghent University (2022, attested 2026).

Werner Abraham was a linguist who studied at TU Wien, Innsbruck, and the University of Vienna (PhD ~1960–1965). He held posts at Illinois, Tübingen, and Groningen (ordinary professor from 1971), with visiting professorships at Cologne, Vienna, Lund, and Munich.

Werner Georg Kümmel was a religious studies scholar. He held academic posts at the University of Zurich (~1932–1951), Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (~1951–1952), and the University of Marburg (~1952–1973).
Werner Handt was an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Tübingen in 1900 under the doctoral supervision of Richard von Garbe.
Werner Knobl is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Paul Thieme. He served as a lecturer at Kyoto University (attested 2001–2007).

Werner Schulemann specialized in Tibetology and other fields. He earned degrees at Breslau (Dr.phil., 1909–1913) and Freiburg (Dr.med., 1909–1914), worked at IG Farben (~1925–1936), and was a professor at Düsseldorf (1931) and Bonn (1938–1955).

Werner Sundermann specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1967), the Academy of Sciences of the GDR (~1970–1991), and the Free University of Berlin (~1993–2000).
